evidence.correctness: Fetched the pinned ORFS liberty files (accel-pdkprice/fetch_pdk.sh + sparse-checkout gf180) into the scratchpad, reran experiments/run.py in a copy: results.txt and results.json byte/value identical to the committed ones. Hand-recomputed from the raw SKY130 tt_025C_1v80 Liberty text (not lib.py): dlclkp_1 CLK fall mean 0.020042 + rise mean 0.006166 + 0.004151 pF x 1.8^2 = 0.013449 -> 39.66 fJ, matches 39.7. GF180 7t 3.3 V icgtp_1 (!E&!TE): 0.17352 + 0.10834 + 0.006772 x 3.3^2 -> 0.3556 pJ, matches. Recomputed every G* = ceil(e_icg/(e_weight x ratio)) from data/ and results.json: all 64 match, 63 of 64 cells <= 24, max 27, 35 flips. Leakage 0.00844 nW x 10 ns = 8.4e-5 fJ matches the README's 0.0001 fJ. Two model-level errors in reported numbers: (1) a gated WS needs a gate on all B accumulators per lane (the written one rotates), so per cycle P=8 more gates are clocked than the model charges (it gates only the (B-1) extra accumulators); with that term the G=24 thresholds rise from 0.080 to 0.159 pJ (64x70, B=2; 2x) and 0.117 to 0.233 (11x64, B=2), G*<=24 drops to 62/64 and max G* to 29. Verdict direction survives. (2) Table means are unweighted over input slews up to 8.6 ns in GF180; at the smallest characterised slew (0.02 ns) dffq_1 is 0.247 pJ (7t 3.3 V) not 0.350, 0.789 not 1.256 (9t 5 V), so the '7.5 to 27 times SKY130' line is ~5.3 to 17 at realistic clock slew. The ICG/flop ratio stays ~1 (0.993-0.999).
evidence.completeness: Every result claimed in the README is produced by experiments/run.py and reproduced exactly from the pinned PDK fetch (SKY130 table, G grid 1..576, G* table, node-free table, GF180 flop/gate ratios). Figure script exists (not run, matplotlib optional). The 9 tests run (8 pass, 1 skips without the PDK). Next steps (RTL, enable logic, GF180 SRAM) are honestly listed as not done.
evidence.verification: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` -> 'Ran 9 tests ... OK (skipped=1)'. Three seeded mutations via quality_mutate.py: C*V -> C*V^2 in lib.py caught; averaging over when-groups replaced by max (lib.py:82) survived because the fixture's two groups have equal energy; packing divisor width//4 -> width//8 in run.py:74 survived because no test reruns the experiment (test_results_consistent only checks the committed JSON). The 'one fewer flop per gate does not win' assertion at tests/test_gatedprice.py:68 adds a slack of 8.44e-5 pJ (84 fJ) where the leakage is 8.44e-8 pJ: a 1000x unit slip that makes the G*-1 half of the test vacuous (c(G*-1) is 1.5 to 40 fJ). The only real-library test skips by default.
evidence.craft: Read lib.py (102 lines), run.py (98), test file (83). Small, readable, stdlib only, units asserted against the Liberty header. Defects: regex Liberty parsing (fragile but checked against one real cell); `_table_mean` returns the list not a mean; leakage re-parsed with a separate regex in run.py instead of lib's cell_leakage; the README's G* formula subtracts leakage but run.py's leakage floor is only the flop's while e_icg also adds the ICG's leakage (consistent but undocumented).
evidence.claims: Backed: 39.7 vs 46.4 fJ, ratios 0.855/0.925 and 0.988-1.018, thresholds 2.2..17.8 pJ ungated, 35 of 64 flips, max G* 27, packed 0.84-2.85 pJ (stated 0.8-2.9), 1/ratio 48-385 and 71-560 flop-cycles. Not backed or misleading: 'with its enable low' for SKY130 dlclkp (its CLK pin has one internal_power group with no when, so the GATE state is not known); 'Against the packed SKY130 macros ... 63 of the 64 ... cells' mixes the 32 packed cells with the 64 total (packed: 31 of 32); 'No cell lacks a winning G' is true by construction (G->inf leaves only 0.0001 fJ leakage) and is presented as a finding; GF180 '7.5 to 27 times' is inflated by the slew-mean (above); the per-flop gated cost omits the active accumulator's gate without saying so (the limitations list omits enable logic and the gate's switching when enabled, not the missing P gates). No clock-gating literature cited.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can rerun it (pinned commit, stdlib, reproduces exactly) and build on the G* table. But the main finding (one ICG idles at about one flop's clock cost, so gating pays once a gate covers a few flops) is standard practice: synthesis tools' clock-gating minimum bit-width default is about 3 bits for this reason, and gated-clock register files are textbook (Benini and De Micheli, gated clocks; Eyeriss gates idle PEs). The project does not cite or compare with this, and the 'flips the accel-pdkprice verdict' framing overstates novelty: accel-pdkprice itself already said gating makes the flop term near zero. No clock tree / wire, where gating saves most, is modelled.
evidence.domain: Compared with how an ISLPED/MICRO reviewer would cost clock gating: (a) gate count should be B*P per array (every accumulator, active one included), not (B-1)*P; (b) Liberty internal power should be looked up at the design's clock slew (or a CTS-reported slew), not averaged across 0.02-8.6 ns; (c) the gated design moves the clock-tree leaf load behind the ICG, which is the dominant saving in practice and is left out on both sides; (d) enabled-ICG energy and enable-logic toggling per write are omitted (acknowledged). The ICG-to-flop ratio being ~1 is robust to (b), and the WS-wins verdict survives (a) on these numbers, so the direction is likely right, but the thresholds a reader would quote are understated up to 2x.

defects.what: Gated cost charges one ICG per extra flop-group only ((B-1)*P gates); a gated WS must gate all B accumulators per lane since the written one rotates, so P more gates clock every cycle. Thresholds at G=24 are understated up to 2x (0.080 -> 0.159 pJ at 64x70 B=2), G*<=24 falls 63 -> 62/64, max G* 27 -> 29. Not in Limitations.

Liberty internal-power tables are averaged unweighted across all input slews (GF180 up to 8.6 ns), inflating GF180 flop/gate energies 30-60% (dffq_1 7t 3.3 V 0.350 vs 0.247 pJ at 0.02 ns slew); README's '7.5 to 27 times SKY130' is ~5.3 to 17 at realistic clock slew. Ratio unaffected.
Test tolerance unit slip: adds 8.44e-5 pJ (84 fJ) where the leakage is 8.44e-8 pJ, making the 'G*-1 does not win' check vacuous.

No test reruns the experiment logic (packing divisor mutant survives) and the group-averaging is untested because the fixture's two when-groups have equal energy (max() mutant survives); the real-library test skips by default.
README says the SKY130 ICG is read 'with its enable low', but dlclkp_1's CLK pin has one internal_power group with no when condition.

'Against the packed SKY130 macros ... wins in 63 of the 64 cells' mixes the packed subset (31 of 32) with the all-cell count; 'No cell lacks a winning G' is true by construction (G->inf leaves only leakage).

No clock-gating prior work cited (synthesis minimum gating bit-width, Benini/De Micheli gated clocks, Eyeriss gating); the 'flips the verdict' framing overstates novelty since accel-pdkprice already concluded gating removes the flop term. Clock tree/leaf wire, where gating saves most, is excluded on both sides.

verdict: A small, reproducible Liberty-reading study: rerunning against the pinned ORFS PDK reproduces results.txt exactly, and hand recomputation of the SKY130 dlclkp_1 (39.7 fJ) and GF180 icgtp_1 (0.356 pJ) idle energies and all 64 G* values matches. The robust finding (an idle ICG costs about one idle flop in both nodes, so a gate shared by G flops cuts idle cost about G-fold) is textbook clock-gating practice and is not compared with that literature. The cost model gates only the extra accumulators, missing the P gates on the active accumulators, which understates the G=24 thresholds up to 2x (the WS-wins direction survives), and unweighted slew averaging inflates the GF180 absolute energies 30-60%. Tests are thin (2 of 3 seeded mutants survive, a 1000x unit slip in a tolerance). Below the bar on correctness, claims and verification.
